metadata.name: TB6612 Dual Motor Driver
metadata.description: Dual H-bridge motor driver for controlling two DC motors or one stepper motor, 1.2A per channel
metadata.author: Adafruit

connectionGuide.purpose: Power supply for the motors. This should be your motor battery/power supply, NOT the Pico's 3.3V.
warnings: Motor voltage range: 4.5V to 13.5V
Do NOT connect to Pico 3.3V - motors need separate power
Ensure adequate current capacity for your motors
troubleshooting: If motors don't spin: check VM power connection and voltage
If motors are weak: ensure power supply can provide enough current

connectionGuide.purpose: Logic level power for the driver chip. Connect to Pico 3.3V.
warnings: Logic voltage range: 2.7V to 5.5V
Connect to Pico 3.3V for proper logic levels
troubleshooting: If control signals don't work: verify VCC connection to 3.3V

connectionGuide.purpose: Common ground for both logic and motor power. Must connect to Pico GND AND motor power supply ground.
warnings: Must share common ground between Pico and motor power supply
Multiple GND pins on board are internally connected
troubleshooting: If erratic behavior: ensure all grounds are connected together

stby.name: STBY
stby.description: Standby pin - pull HIGH to enable outputs

connectionGuide.purpose: Standby control. Must be HIGH for motors to operate. Can connect to VCC for always-on, or to a GPIO for power saving.
warnings: Motors will NOT run if STBY is LOW
For simple use: connect directly to VCC (3.3V)
troubleshooting: If motors don't run: check STBY is pulled HIGH
Can use GPIO to enable/disable driver for power saving

connectionGuide.purpose: Direction control for Motor A. Combined with AIN2: (1,0)=forward, (0,1)=reverse, (0,0)=coast, (1,1)=brake
warnings: Connect to any GPIO pin
troubleshooting: If motor spins wrong direction: swap AIN1 and AIN2 logic

connectionGuide.purpose: Direction control for Motor A. Used with AIN1 to set direction.
warnings: Connect to any GPIO pin

connectionGuide.purpose: Speed control for Motor A. Use PWM signal to control motor speed (0-100% duty cycle).
warnings: Connect to a PWM-capable GPIO pin
100% duty cycle = full speed, 0% = stopped
troubleshooting: If motor doesn't respond to speed changes: verify PWM signal with oscilloscope or LED

connectionGuide.purpose: Direction control for Motor B. Combined with BIN2: (1,0)=forward, (0,1)=reverse, (0,0)=coast, (1,1)=brake
warnings: Connect to any GPIO pin
troubleshooting: If motor spins wrong direction: swap BIN1 and BIN2 logic

connectionGuide.purpose: Direction control for Motor B. Used with BIN1 to set direction.
warnings: Connect to any GPIO pin

connectionGuide.purpose: Speed control for Motor B. Use PWM signal to control motor speed.
warnings: Connect to a PWM-capable GPIO pin

connectionGuide.purpose: Connect to one terminal of Motor A.
warnings: Maximum 1.2A continuous current per channel

connectionGuide.purpose: Connect to other terminal of Motor A.
Connect to one terminal of Motor B.
warnings: Maximum 1.2A continuous current per channel

connectionGuide.purpose: Connect to other terminal of Motor B.

warnings: Motor power (VM) and logic power (VCC) are separate - don't mix them
STBY pin must be HIGH for motors to operate
Maximum 1.2A continuous per motor channel
Ensure motor power supply can provide adequate current
Share common ground between Pico and motor power supply
usageNotes: Speed control: PWM duty cycle on PWMA/PWMB (0-100%)
STBY: Connect to VCC for always-on, or use GPIO for power management
Can drive 2 DC motors or 1 bipolar/unipolar stepper motor
